headline: High-risk default write/egress orchestration: n8n can ingest and act on mem0-derived content, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls, while n8n can read/write the server filesystem and call workflow nodes. If mem0 content is fed into n8n workflows, attacker-controlled text can be treated as instructions. The pathway is plausible in default integrations, though not proven.
conditions: IF mem0 outputs are ingested into an n8n workflow without provenance filtering
IF n8n nodes parse mem0-sourced text as instructions or parameters
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to mem0 outputs before workflow ingestion
Insert a manual approval step before any n8n action node
Restrict n8n parsers to structured JSON only
Disable automatic execution of text-derived commands
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and schema validation at the workflow boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: mem0 is a memory store, and n8n has broad network egress plus filesystem access. If the workflow processes sensitive data, n8n can transmit it to external integrations or persist it on the server, while mem0 may retain it as long-term memory. That creates a default exfiltration/retention risk with sensitive workflow data.
conditions: IF the workflow processes secrets, customer data, or personal data
IF n8n integration nodes send that data to third-party services
IF mem0 stores the same data class as persistent memory
mitigations: Limit n8n credentials to least-privilege scopes
Exclude sensitive fields before mem0 storage
Turn off verbose workflow logging
Review every outbound integration node for data handling
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction and retention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: mem0 is a shared memory layer, and n8n supports multiple instances with shared state via datastore and connected systems. n8n also has server filesystem write access and shell execution, so concurrent workflows can overwrite shared artifacts or race on mutable state. The overlap is broad enough to make write conflicts dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared datastore, file path, or memory namespace
IF multiple n8n executions run concurrently against the same resource
mitigations: Assign separate namespaces per workflow
Serialize writes with a lock or queue
Avoid shared filesystem paths for intermediate artifacts
Disable shell writes for workflows that touch shared state
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is an action-taking orchestrator, and mem0 can supply remembered context that workflows may treat as authoritative. If n8n consumes mem0 output without verification, a mistaken or stale memory entry can cascade into external actions such as API calls, emails, or database updates. The interaction is default-dangerous because n8n is built to execute downstream steps.
conditions: IF n8n uses mem0 output as a decision input without a verification step
IF downstream workflow nodes perform external side effects based on that input
mitigations: Add a human review gate before side-effecting nodes
Require source citations for any mem0-derived claim
Compare mem0 output against a second source
Log and diff memory reads before execution
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rollback handling

E_compliance.rationale: mem0 is a memory system, while n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and can send it to many integrations. If regulated data enters n8n, retention and residency obligations can diverge between persistent memory and workflow logs/credentials. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or secrets are processed by the workflow
IF n8n retention or logging exceeds the policy applied to mem0 memory
mitigations: Document the data classes allowed in the workflow
Shorten log retention in n8n
Exclude regulated fields from memory writes
Review credential storage settings
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems
